name: Classification / Odd One Out
shortcutSummary: Find the common property shared by all but one item. The odd one out is the item that does NOT share that property. Always check at least two possible groupings before finalizing.
conceptExplanation:
Classification or Odd One Out questions ask you to identify the item that does not belong to a group. The group shares a common property — it could be based on meaning, category, mathematical property, or pattern. Your job is to find what unites the majority and which item breaks that unity.

These questions appear in every major exam: SSC, Banking, Railways, and Defence. They test your ability to categorize and spot the outlier quickly.

subtopics.name: Word-based Classification
subtopics.explanation: Group words by category, property, or meaning. The odd one is the word that belongs to a different category or lacks the shared property.
shortcuts: Category Check: Identify what category most items belong to (fruits, animals, countries, etc.). The odd one is from a different category.
Property Check: If category is the same, check for a sub-property (e.g., all are mammals except one reptile).
Semantic Relationship: Sometimes the link is not category but relationship (all synonyms except one antonym).

examples.questionText: Find the odd one out: Apple, Mango, Potato, Banana
examples.solutionSteps: Apple, Mango, Banana are fruits. Potato is a vegetable. Answer: Potato

examples.questionText: Find the odd one out: January, March, June, July
examples.solutionSteps: January (31 days), March (31 days), July (31 days) — all have 31 days. June has only 30 days. Answer: June

examples.questionText: Find the odd one out: Surgeon, Physician, Carpenter, Dentist
examples.solutionSteps: Surgeon, Physician, Dentist are all medical professionals. Carpenter is not. Answer: Carpenter

examples.questionText: Find the odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Moon, Mars
examples.solutionSteps: Mercury, Venus, Mars are planets. Moon is a natural satellite, not a planet. Answer: Moon

examples.questionText: Find the odd one out: Braille, Morse, Sanskrit, Semaphore
examples.solutionSteps: Braille, Morse, and Semaphore are all communication codes/systems. Sanskrit is a language, not a code system. Answer: Sanskrit

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Dog, Cat, Cow, Rose
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Dog, Cat, Cow are animals. Rose is a flower. Answer: Rose.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: 11, 13, 15, 17, 19
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: 11, 13, 17, 19 are prime numbers. 15 = 3×5 is not prime. Answer: 15.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Mercury, Jupiter, Pluto, Saturn
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn are planets. Pluto is a dwarf planet (reclassified in 2006). Answer: Pluto.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: 8=2³, 27=3³, 64=4³, 125=5³ are perfect cubes. 100=10² is not a perfect cube. Answer: 100.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Circle, Hexagon
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Hexagon are polygons (have straight sides). Circle has no straight sides. Answer: Circle.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Potato, Carrot, Ginger, Apple
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Potato, Carrot, Ginger are root vegetables. Apple is a fruit. Answer: Apple.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, Eiffel Tower, Red Fort
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, Red Fort are monuments in India. Eiffel Tower is in France. Answer: Eiffel Tower.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: 2, 3, 5, 9, 11
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: 2, 3, 5, 11 are prime numbers. 9 = 3×3 is not prime. Answer: 9.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Tennis, Cricket, Hockey, Chess
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Tennis, Cricket, Hockey are outdoor sports involving physical movement. Chess is an indoor board game. Answer: Chess.
144=12², 169=13², 196=14², 225=15² are perfect squares. 260 is not a perfect square. Answer: 260.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Walk, Run, Sit, Jog
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Walk, Run, Jog all involve forward movement/locomotion. Sit does not involve movement. Answer: Sit.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: January, May, July, November
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: January (31), May (31), July (31) have 31 days. November has 30 days. Answer: November.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Sparrow, Parrot, Bat, Eagle
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Sparrow, Parrot, Eagle are birds. Bat is a mammal (despite flying). Answer: Bat.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Iron, Gold, Mercury, Copper
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Iron, Gold, Copper are solid metals at room temperature. Mercury is the only liquid metal at room temperature. Answer: Mercury.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Whale, Shark, Dolphin, Crocodile
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Whale, Dolphin are marine mammals. Crocodile is a reptile. Shark is a fish. Among aquatic animals: Whale, Shark, Dolphin live in oceans. Crocodile lives in rivers/freshwater. OR: Whale, Dolphin, Crocodile breathe air (lungs). Shark breathes through gills. Answer depends on grouping. Most common answer: Shark (only fish, rest are non-fish).

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: 121, 143, 169, 196
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: 121=11², 169=13², 196=14² are perfect squares. 143=11×13 is not a perfect square. Answer: 143.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Mediterranean
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian are oceans. Mediterranean is a sea, not an ocean. Answer: Mediterranean.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: 1, 8, 27, 65, 125
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: 1=1³, 8=2³, 27=3³, 125=5³ are perfect cubes. 65 is not a perfect cube (4³=64, not 65). Answer: 65.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Nile, Amazon, Sahara, Ganges
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Nile, Amazon, Ganges are rivers. Sahara is a desert. Answer: Sahara.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: Keyboard, Mouse, CPU, Printer
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: Keyboard, Mouse are input devices. Printer is an output device. CPU is a processing unit (neither input nor output device). OR: Keyboard, Mouse, Printer are peripheral devices. CPU is the central processing unit. Answer: CPU.

subtopics.name: Number-based Classification
subtopics.explanation: Group numbers by mathematical property: prime, even/odd, perfect square, divisibility, digit sum, etc.
shortcuts: Prime Check First: Check if all numbers are prime — the non-prime is the odd one.
Square/Cube Check: Check if numbers are perfect squares or cubes.
Divisibility Pattern: Check if all are divisible by a common factor.

examples.solutionSteps: 2, 5, 7, 11 are prime numbers. 9 = 3×3 is not prime. Answer: 9
16=4², 25=5², 36=6², 64=8² are perfect squares. 45 is not a perfect square. Answer: 45

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: 4, 9, 16, 24, 36
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: 4=2², 9=3², 16=4², 36=6² are perfect squares. 24 is not. Answer: 24.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Find the odd one out: 3, 6, 9, 14, 15
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps: 3, 6, 9, 15 are all divisible by 3. 14 is not divisible by 3. Answer: 14.
